findings.problem: Prop drop flight trajectories evaluate original release hands at original-run relative time (g.releaseMs) inside a shot-local context when sourceManipulation is active, misaligning release time and causing infinite recursion or clock mismatch errors.
findings.fix: Strip sourceManipulation from original.plan (or call manipulationSourcePlan(original.plan) with includeProps false) to prevent recursive re-evaluation of source manipulation contexts during samplePerformanceState, and map g.releaseMs to the exact run-relative time (e.g. g.releaseMs + plan.sourceManipulation.startMs - original.clock.runStartMs) when evaluating original release hand positions.

findings.problem: resolvedGesture in samplePerformanceState passes entryTimeMs to expressiveArmReference as an absolute run-relative time instead of a plan-local time, causing bodyStateAt to sample body posture/locomotion out of shot bounds when resolving gesture entry references.
findings.evidence:
In compiler.ts:786-787:
entryTimeMs:source?source.startMs-actingClock!.startMs:contact?contact.startMs+plan.sourceManipulation!.startMs-actingClock!.startMs:gesture?.startMs??0
For contact, entryTimeMs is computed as contact.startMs + plan.sourceManipulation.startMs - actingClock.startMs. This offset is shot-relative, but expressiveArmReference invokes bodyStateAt(plan, profile, entryTimeMs, actingClock). Inside bodyStateAt, when actingClock is present, actingClock expects time to be relative to the shot (0 to plan.durationMs) or global run time consistently. If contact starts prior to actingClock.startMs (e.g., in a preceding camera cut of the continuous run), entryTimeMs becomes negative, violating non-negative time bounds or clamp in bodyStateAt.

findings.fix: Ensure entryTimeMs passed to expressiveArmReference is evaluated in original source run space consistently when actingClock is supplied, or clamp/project entryTimeMs to the causal entry frame within the run clock rather than producing negative shot-relative timestamps.

findings.problem: sourceManipulationGestureAt boundary condition at duration strictly matches only carry gestures with releaseMs===undefined, dropping contact gestures whose endMs aligns with slice boundaries.

findings.fix: Allow at === duration && g.endMs === duration for all continuous contact gestures that span to the end of the duration.

findings.problem: Critical contact transition times in compiler.ts use undefined constants CARRY_TRANSITION_MS without fallback, and offset calculation does not protect against missing actingClock.

findings.fix: Guard actingClock with (actingClock ? plan.sourceManipulation.startMs - actingClock.startMs : 0) and ensure CARRY_TRANSITION_MS is properly imported from native contact schemas/constants.

limitations: No execution, render, test pipeline, or runtime samplers were executed; findings are static defect analysis based on provided source code.

dispositions.reason: validateViewSourceManipulation requires source.startMs===clock.runStartMs and endMs===runEndMs; originalManipulationContext validates that before expanding the frame. g.releaseMs is therefore correctly run-relative in the expanded plan. includeProps=false makes the entire prop loop empty on recursive palm evaluation, so no second flight evaluation or context recursion occurs. Retaining sourceManipulation is required to resolve the original gesture; stripping it would lose that hand command. This is source reasoning, not runtime proof.

Entry offset is intentionally shot-local and may be negative. bodyStateAt does not clamp it to a shot; with sourceBody it computes motionTime=entryTimeMs+clock.startMs-sourceBody.startMs, which equals the valid original contact.startMs because the source spans match. Original global emotion/body/head history is retained. Clamping to the cut would restart the arm reference. Existing point/think source references already use this causal negative shot offset. Original head-cell/voice entry and bank-specific behavior still needs real tests.

Released contact commands use half-open active windows and have completed recovery at their end; returning rest at the exact final end matches gestureAt and sourceViewGestureAt semantics. Only an unreleased carry must retain ownership at the scene-exit endpoint, which is explicitly preserved. All original props remain sampled even after their gesture ended, so destination/flight is not lost. No geometry/video acceptance is inferred.

CARRY_TRANSITION_MS is a module constant250 at compiler line79, outside the partial excerpt. compilePerformance rejects sourceBody without complete actingClock before event collection; sourceManipulation also requires matching sourceBody. samplePerformanceState separately requires its owned clock. A zero-offset fallback would hide missing context and is not accepted.
